results.name: small_vs_large_region_gap
results.description: Among targets outside the span by a linear gap of 5-40, yes-rate when the nearest example is <=20 minus when the nearest example is >=60; observed < null means people compress large numbers (log-like magnitude) so equal linear gaps matter more among small numbers, which the linear-distance model fails to produce.

results.name: exact_example_target_yes
results.description: Yes-rate on trials whose target is one of the shown examples, minus yes-rate on targets within 1-3 of the nearest example; observed > null means people treat a repeated example as near-certainly produced far more than nearby numbers, and the model under-produces this boost.

results.name: sample_size_breadth_contrast
results.description: Among targets outside the examples' span by 5-40, yes-rate for four-example sets minus yes-rate for one-example sets; observed < null means people narrow generalization with more examples (size principle) more than the model does, observed > null the reverse.
results.code:
# name: sample_size_breadth_contrast
# description: Among targets outside the examples' span by 5-40, yes-rate for four-example sets minus yes-rate for one-example sets; observed < null means people narrow generalization with more examples (size principle) more than the model does, observed > null the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    k = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.count(",") + 1
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    mn = ex.map(lambda e: min(int(x) for x in e))
    mx = ex.map(lambda e: max(int(x) for x in e))
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    gap = np.maximum(np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx), 0)
    sel = (gap >= 5) & (gap <= 40)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    a = r[sel & (k == 4)]
    b = r[sel & (k == 1)]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())

results.name: parity_violation_contrast
results.description: For sets of >=2 examples that all share one parity, yes-rate on opposite-parity targets minus same-parity targets; observed < null means people reject parity-violating targets more strongly than the model's graded parity similarity produces (observed > null: model over-penalizes parity).
results.code:
# name: parity_violation_contrast
# description: For sets of >=2 examples that all share one parity, yes-rate on opposite-parity targets minus same-parity targets; observed < null means people reject parity-violating targets more strongly than the model's graded parity similarity produces (observed > null: model over-penalizes parity).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    k = ex.str.len()
    odd = ex.map(lambda e: sum(int(x) % 2 for x in e))
    allsame = (k >= 2) & ((odd == 0) | (odd == k))
    setpar = (odd == k).astype(int)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    viol = (t % 2) != setpar
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    a = r[allsame & viol]
    b = r[allsame & ~viol]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())

results.name: first_vs_last_example_proximity
results.description: In sets of >=2 examples, among non-example targets within 1-10 of their nearest example, yes-rate when that nearest example was shown first minus when it was shown last; observed > null means people weight the first example (primacy) more than the model's recency-weighted memory allows, observed < null means recency is stronger than modelled.

results.name: math_category_match_contrast
results.description: For sets of >=2 examples that all belong to a mathematical category the model does not represent (perfect squares, powers of two, cubes, primes), yes-rate on targets inside that category minus yes-rate on targets outside it; observed > null means people use these categories and the model under-produces category-based generalization.

results.name: same_decade_near_contrast
results.description: Among targets outside the example set lying within 1-10 of their nearest example, yes-rate when the target shares that example's tens decade minus when it does not; observed > null means people use decade membership (which the model, with only size and final digit, lacks) and the model under-produces this contrast.

results.name: within_set_target_spread
results.description: For sets asked with >=8 distinct targets, the mean over sets of the SD of per-target yes-rates across targets; observed > null means people discriminate between targets of the same set more sharply than the model (model too smooth), observed < null means the model is too sharp.
